'''Alfonso Martínez Arias''' is a Spanish and British developmental biologist known by his pioneering development of gastruloids, a stem cell based embryo model for the study of early human development,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cyranoski |first=David |date=2020-06-11 |title=Lab-grown cells mimic crucial moment in embryo development |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-01757-z |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=582 |issue=7812 |pages=325 |doi=10.1038/d41586-020-01757-z |pmid=32546866 |bibcode=2020Natur.582..325C |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-12 |title='Embryo-like' model mimics crucial period of human development |url=https://www.sciencefocus.com/news/embryo-like-model-mimics-crucial-period-of-human-development |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=BBC Science Focus Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Callier |first=Viviane |title=Small Collections of Cells Determine How a Body Takes Its Shape |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/small-collections-of-cells-determine-how-a-body-takes-its-shape/ |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Domínguez |first=Nuño |title=Un modelo de embrión humano muestra una fase nunca observada de la vida the need to look at biology from the perspective of the cell rather than the gene.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Horwitz |first1=Rick |title=The new cell theory <b>The Master Builder</b> == Early life and education ==
Martínez Arias was born in Madrid, Spain. He obtained his undergraduate degree in biology from the [[Complutense University of Madrid|Universidad Complutense de Madrid]] in 1977 and in 1978 moved to the US with a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] fellowship where he completed his PhD in 1983 at the Department of Biophysics and Theoretical Biology of the [[University of Chicago]], Chicago (US) under the supervision of [[Malcolm Casadaban]].

== Academic career ==
After postdoctoral research at the [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in Cambridge, United Kingdom, he became a [[Wellcome Trust]] Senior Fellow in the Department of Zoology at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He later joined the Department of Genetics at Cambridge, where he was appointed professor of developmental mechanics in 2003 and remained until 2021. In 2021 he moved to Barcelona to become an ICREA research professor in the Systems Bioengineering/Experimental and Health Sciences programmes at UPF and the [[Barcelona Biomedical Research Park|Barcelona Biomedical Research Park (PRBB)]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfonso Martínez Arias, new ICREA Senior researcher at UPF - Focus UPF - UPF |url=https://www.upf.edu/web/focus/noticies/-/asset_publisher/qOocsyZZDGHL/content/alfonso-martinez-arias-nuevo-investigador-icrea-senior-en-la-upf/10193 |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=Focus UPF |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Martínez Arias's research focuses on how a fertilized egg gives rise to an organized organism, with particular emphasis on the early stages of mammalian development. His work has combined drosophila developmental genetics with embryonic stem cell biology to study cell fate heterogeneity, signalling networks, and self‑organization. His laboratory developed “[[Gastruloid|gastruloids]]”, three‑dimensional aggregates of [[Cell potency|pluripotent]] [[Stem cell|stem cells]] that recapitulate key features of vertebrate gastrulation In addition to his research publications, Martínez Arias is co‑author of the textbook ''Molecular Principles of Animal Development''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Vincent |first=Jean-Paul |date=November 2002 |title=Developmental biology turned on its head |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/ncb1102-e257 |journal=Nature Cell Biology |language=en |volume=4 |issue=11 |article-number=E257 |doi=10.1038/ncb1102-e257 |issn=1476-4679|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and of ''Principles of Development''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/wolperts-principles-of-development-9780192896612?cc=es&lang=en& |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=global.oup.com | title=Wolpert's Principles of Development}}</ref> a widely used developmental biology textbook that has reached its seventh edition and received the [[Royal Society of Biology]] book prize.

He is also the author of the popular science book ''The Master Builder''  published in 2023,<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/alfonso-martinez-arias/the-master-builder-science-cell/ |title=THE MASTER BUILDER {{!}} Kirkus Reviews |language=en}}</ref> where he argues that to understand life we must put '''cells''', ''not'' genes, at the center of biology, that while DNA provides a catalogue of parts, it is cells that interpret this information, interact with each other, and build bodies during development. The book develops a “cell's‑eye view” of organisms and challenges popular “[[Selfish genetic element|selfish gene]]” narratives and proposes a new paradigm rooted in cellular cooperation, with implications for how we think about evolution, individuality, development, disease, and the ethical questions raised by embryo and stem‑cell research.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ansede |first=Manuel |date=2024-05-08 |title=La fusión de dos hermanas en una única mujer sugiere que la identidad del ser humano no está en su ADN |url=https://elpais.com/ciencia/2024-05-08/la-fusion-de-dos-hermanas-en-una-unica-mujer-sugiere-que-la-identidad-del-ser-humano-no-esta-en-su-adn.html |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=El País |language=es}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Martínez Arias was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 2007<ref name=":2" /> and of the [[Academia Europaea|Academia Europea]] in 2025.<ref name=":3" /> In 2012 he received the [[Waddington Medal]] from the [[British Society for Developmental Biology]] for his contributions to developmental biology<ref name=":4" />  and in 2016 a live achievement award from the [[Society of Spanish Researchers in the United Kingdom|Society of Spanish Researchers]] in the UK<ref>{{Cite web |title=SRUK/CERU Merit Award |url=https://sruk.org.uk/initiatives/funding-grants-awards/sruk-merit-award/ |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=Society of Spanish Researchers in the United Kingdom |language=en-GB}}</ref>

His research has been supported by grants from Advanced Grants from the Wellcome Trust, the [[European Research Council]] and the [[Human Frontier Science Program]] grant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cambridge researchers win European Research Council funding {{!}} Cambridge Network |url=https://www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk/news/cambridge-researchers-win-european-research-council-funding |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=www.cambridgenetwork.co.uk}}</ref>
